collection.title: Astrocytic sEH-EET signaling regulates microglial lysosomal function and suppresses the STING-Type I interferon pathway in Alzheimer's disease
collection.authors: Ghosh, B.; Wang, S.; Qi, C.; Ghosh, A.; Comerota, M.; Rajpurohit, C. S.; Zeldin, D. C.; Zheng, H.
collection.abstract: Background: The development of {beta}-amyloid (A{beta}) pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is accompanied by profound changes in astrocytes and microglia and associated neuroinflammation. Soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH), which degrades anti-inflammatory epoxyeicosatrienoic acids (EETs), is elevated in the AD brain, yet how EETs restrain inflammation remains poorly understood. Methods: We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on brains from wild-type, sEH knockout, 5xFAD, and 5xFAD; sEH knockout mice, and used primary mouse microglia and human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived microglia to define the underlying mechanism. To test cell-type-specific contributions, we generated astrocyte- and endothelial-specific she knockout mice and crossed them with 5xFAD mice. Results: Genetic disruption of sEH in 5xFAD mice markedly reduced the abundance of a type I interferon (IFN)-responsive microglial subcluster and lowered phospho-STING (pSTING) levels. In primary microglia, supplementation with 11,12-EET attenuated STING activation and IFN target gene expression; blocking lysosomal acidification abolished this effect and caused pSTING to accumulate, identifying lysosomal degradation as a critical route for terminating STING signaling. 11,12-EET also enhanced microglial lysosomal acidification and A{beta} phagocytosis. Astrocytic, but not endothelial, disruption of sEH recapitulated the reductions in A{beta} pathology and microglial STING activation seen in global sEH-deficient mice, identifying astrocytes as the major cellular source of EETs regulating this pathway. Conclusion: We define an astrocyte-microglia axis in which astrocytic sEH limits EET availability and thereby sustains microglial STING signaling. By promoting lysosomal clearance of pSTING, EETs suppress type I IFN signaling and enhance microglial A{beta} clearance, highlighting sEH inhibition as a therapeutic strategy targeting both neuroinflammation and lysosomal dysfunction in AD.
